Q: Is there a better way to distribute a .NET 10 application with a custom local runtime? A:

For most .NET 10 applications, a self-contained deployment is probably the simplest option because it includes the required runtime and users don't need to install .NET separately. A custom local runtime can work, but it may make updates and maintenance more complicated. https://gachanebulaapk.app/

Q: Where is the C Standard function sqrt actually defined? (Windows user) A:

Where is the C Standard function sqrt actually defined?

The C23 spec has 7.12.7.10 The sqrt functions

double sqrt(double x);

The sqrt functions compute the nonnegative square root of x. A domain error occurs if the argument is less than zero.
The sqrt functions return √ x.

about how it is defined inside the C Standard Library and my machine.

An implementation may use additional keywords. C does not, itself specify how or even how well the square root is implemented.

Even if today, one reviews the source code of an implementation, a subsequent version is not obligate to perform like a pervious one.

Yet sqrt(x) is a very well understood function. A quality sqrt() is readily achievable and expected in 2026. So good the result is expected to be the best result.

Of note, an implementation that follows IEEE 754, sqrt(-0.0) is -0.0 which somewhat goes against compute the nonnegative square root of x.

Q: How to achieve a blur effect in PHP? A:

I've tried many answers, but I've obtained best results and best scalability with the Imagick PHP extension. Example PHP code:

$imagick = new Imagick('a.jpeg');
$imagick->blurImage(0, 6.0); // Radius, sigma
$imagick->writeImage('a.jpeg');
$imagick->clear();

Original image:

To:

To have more blur, just increase the 6.0 sigma parameter.

Disadvantages:

  • you need to install the Imagick extension (sudo apt install php-imagick or similar)

Advantages:

  • more efficient than exec() and convert etc. - as it's native PHP, not a shell command
  • greatly more efficient than calling imagefilter($image, IMG_FILTER_GAUSSIAN_BLUR); multiple times

Credits: https://stackoverflow.com/a/14428602/3451846 https://www.php.net/manual/en/imagick.blurimage.php

Q: C++: Do static primitives become invalid at program exit? A:

To answer your question:

'imagine that the ptr points to some memory address which I want to check in the destructor of some other static class'

The answer is yes.
You can see the value of the pointer (the address).
You can look at the content if you have not called delete on the pointer.

Static function variables behave in the same way as static class variables and global variables (aka non local static), in that there destructors will be called in reverse order of creation. Integers, floats and pointers (POD) do not have destructors so nothing happens to them until the processes is removed.

POD objects: Data can safely by referenced from the destructor of other objects (even global s).

Other static objects (i.e. those with destructors): In the general case, it is not safe to accesses these objects after main() has exited because the order of destruction is not know (it is the reverse of the order of creation, but the order of creation is complex see: Construction Order ). It can be done but you have to take explicit precautions to make sure the object is still alive.

Note: non local static:

The memory will always be there, the object will just not be valid after a destructor is called (note POD does not have a destructor).

Note: Stack:

Only valid until the scope in which they are declared is left.
After the stack is popped the memory page that it is on could potentially be dropped resulting in SEG faults if you attempt to access it.

Note: Heap:

Valid until you call delete on the pointer that allocated it.
Once a pointer is delete the value is potentially random as it may be re-used. Potentially the page the memory was on can also be dropped. Any access to a dropped page would result in a SEG fault.

Q: Find identical aggregated combinations from pivot table in SQL A:

I got this to work, tested on MySQL 9.7. I'll also include a dbfiddle to demo on MySQL 8.0.

WITH en AS (
  SELECT object_tag.tag_id, tag_category_id, name_en, name_es,
    GROUP_CONCAT(object_id ORDER BY object_id ASC) object_ids
  FROM object_tag
  JOIN tags ON (object_tag.tag_id = tags.id)
  WHERE tag_category_id < 10
  GROUP BY object_tag.tag_id
),
es AS (
  SELECT object_tag.tag_id, tag_category_id, name_es,
    GROUP_CONCAT(object_id ORDER BY object_id ASC) object_ids
  FROM object_tag
  JOIN tags ON (object_tag.tag_id = tags.id)
  WHERE tag_category_id > 10
  GROUP BY object_tag.tag_id
),
i AS (
  SELECT en.tag_id, ANY_VALUE(es.name_es) AS name_es
  FROM en
  JOIN es ON (en.object_ids = es.object_ids)
  WHERE en.name_es IS NULL
  AND es.name_es IS NOT NULL
  AND es.tag_category_id = en.tag_category_id + 10
  GROUP BY en.tag_id
  HAVING COUNT(es.tag_id) = 1
)
UPDATE tags t
JOIN i ON t.id = i.tag_id
SET t.name_es = i.name_es;

You almost had it, but the trick is when doing an UPDATE with CTE's, you have to join the CTE back to a concrete table to update.

This might not do all that you need to do, but it demonstrates the technique, and you can adapt it to your needs.

Demo using MySQL 8.0: https://dbfiddle.uk/2OmaBcTD
